analysis: Examined the docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md changes (date bump and an added 'Streaming read' note about the readExactly no-copy behavior) and the SSDBlockStore.swift readExactly patch (lines ~481-501 base/head). The code change removes the up-front reserveCapacity(count). When the first read returns exactly `count` bytes with startIndex == 0, it returns that buffer without copying. Otherwise it reserves capacity and appends, as before. The change does not touch authentication, AES-GCM chunk handling, HMAC lookup tags, AAD, TTL, key handling, or file identity checks. The callers still receive exactly `count` bytes, because the loop continues until out.count reaches count. The startIndex == 0 guard preserves caller zero-indexing, which prevents out-of-range or misindexed reads. Short or truncated reads still throw. The beforeRead budget accounting still runs before each read, with the same charged spans, so the retry raw-byte ceiling and read budget are unchanged. An oversized chunk (chunk.count > count) falls through to append, which is the pre-existing behavior; I could not see the source of the read helper to confirm it never returns more than `count`. Memory impact is neutral or lower (no second buffer copy). I identified no new attack surface relevant to T-041 or TB-007: the at-rest metadata exposure, HMAC naming and TTL remain as documented. Remaining unverified items are outside the supplied evidence: the read helper's maximum return size and whether Data returned from it might be a slice with nonzero startIndex. The guard handles that case safely by falling back to a copy. The doc edits are accurate descriptions and carry no security-control change. The earlier doc text on the threat model is unchanged.
